sections.h2: Where to pay and who sets the bill
sections.html:
Payments go to the Town of Brookhaven Receiver of Taxes during the collection season, December 1 to May 31, and then to the Suffolk County Comptroller. Visit Town Hall at 1 Independence Hill, Farmingville, or call 631-451-9009; the Assessor shares the building. The town runs from Port Jefferson and Stony Brook down to Patchogue and had 485,773 residents in 2020, so school districts and home prices differ widely under a single tax office.

Rates are not the Receiver's decision. Your school district writes the school budget, the county budget drives the county levy, and the Supervisor and Town Board set the town levy.

sections.h2: Tax year and when bills arrive
sections.html:
Suffolk County's tax year starts December 1 and ends November 30 of the next year. The lien attaches on the first day, and the town mails bills in mid-December, aiming for delivery by December 15. Nothing in your mailbox by the third week of December? Phone the tax office.

Each June 1 the online system closes for the year just ended, then reopens in December. Escrowed owners receive an informational copy around mid-July, because the lender is sent the bill to pay.

Half the bill is due January 10, the other half May 31, and one bill may be paid in two parts. Interest on the first half climbs monthly after January 10. Anything unpaid after May 31 is delinquent.

Payment madeInterest added on the first half
January 11 to February 101%
February 11 to March 102%
March 11 to April 103%
April 11 to May 104%
May 11 to May 315%

Enhanced STAR recipients and owners with the over-65 exemption get five additional business days after May 31. After that, the Suffolk County Comptroller handles the account, charging a 5 percent penalty and 1 percent monthly interest running from February 1. The town stays out of delinquent accounts.

Options are online, in person and mail, and postmarks decide a lot. Since a federal change on December 24, 2025, a letter dropped in a mailbox may not be stamped that day. Only a hand-stamped envelope from a post office counter is guaranteed by the town, and penalties cannot be waived when the postmark is late.

  • Online: e-check for $1.75, or a credit card with a 2.35 percent fee. Partial payments are not allowed online.
  • Drop box: outside the Town Hall front lobby, always open, no cash. A receipt follows by mail the next business day.
  • Walk-in: weekdays, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
  • Mail: send the right stub with the check, postmarked by January 10 for the first half and May 31 for the second half.

Either office accepts a partial payment of at least $200 plus interest due. A bounced check adds $20.

Grievances are taken from May 1 until Grievance Day, the third Tuesday of May, which in 2027 is May 18. The online form is open for that same stretch. Exemption applications are due by the March 1 taxable status date. The tentative roll appears May 1 and the final roll July 1.

A paper grievance goes to the Town of Brookhaven Assessor, Attention: Grievance, at 1 Independence Hill, or into the Assessor's bin at the main lobby security desk. Hearings are held at Town Hall on Grievance Day, and the Assessor sometimes adds evening and weekend hours beforehand, so check the Grievance Day page each spring for the schedule.

There is no grace period: anything sent before May 1 or after Grievance Day comes back to you unprocessed.

Under Suffolk County law the owner must pay on time whether or not a bill came, and late payment brings penalties and interest. Because bills mail in December, anyone buying in the county later that year is told to phone the Receiver and verify that every tax is current.

  • Get a current figure from the Receiver, noting if only the first half or the full year is paid
  • Bill sent to an old address? Give the Receiver your correct mailing address
  • After May 31, ask the Suffolk County Comptroller for the payoff. The check address is 330 Center Drive in Riverhead.

Taxes still unpaid at the tax lien sale, which usually happens in December, lead the Comptroller to sell a lien to Suffolk County. A cash buyer can pay off a delinquent balance at closing the same way a lender would, which avoids that sale.

Exemption applications are tied to the March 1 taxable status date, so anything you want on the coming bill needs to be filed by then. Enhanced STAR and the over-65 exemption also carry the extra five business days after May 31 mentioned above. When you sell, tell the new owner which exemptions were in place. They may have to apply on their own, and a buyer who learns that late can end up with a larger bill than expected.

Ask the Assessor, who works from the same Town Hall building as the Receiver, how each exemption is handled when the deed changes hands. Write down the answer and pass it to your closing attorney.

sections.h2: When the bill and the sale overlap
sections.html: Many Brookhaven closings fall between December and May, when one half of the bill may be paid and the other still open. Work out in advance which half you are covering. The same calendar matters if you close after May 31, because the Comptroller, not the town, then holds the account and quotes the payoff. Collecting that figure before the contract is signed prevents a late surprise.

Most Brookhaven homes (80.9 percent) are lived in by their owners. A July 2025 estimate put the population at 496,410, and the median owner-occupied home is worth $489,200, against median gross rent of $2,314. If your assessment seems out of step with comparable houses on your street, contact the Assessor before May.

sections.h2: Closing steps for a cash sale
sections.html:
In a cash deal, title work and payoffs set the pace. Follow this sequence:

  1. Get the current balance from the Receiver, or from the Comptroller after May 31.
  2. Confirm your mailing address is right so no bill goes astray.
  3. Give the figures to your closing attorney or title agent.
  4. Review the closing statement and make sure the tax line matches the number you were given.

Payoffs are deducted from your proceeds, so nothing comes out of pocket. Tell the closing attorney exactly which portions of the year are paid, so the buyer's credit is figured correctly. If a lien sale or delinquency is already on the record, mention it up front, since the payoff is higher after penalties and interest.

faqs.q: When are Brookhaven property taxes due?
faqs.a: Two deadlines: January 10 for the first half, May 31 for the second. Miss the first and you pay another 1 percent per month, reaching 5 percent for payments in the final three weeks of May.

faqs.q: Who do I pay after May 31 in Brookhaven?
faqs.a: The Suffolk County Comptroller, on Center Drive in Riverhead. Expect a 5 percent penalty and 1 percent per month counted from February 1 to be added.

faqs.q: Can I pay Brookhaven tax by credit card?
faqs.a: Online, yes: the card carries a 2.35 percent bank fee, and an e-check is $1.75. The town keeps neither fee, and online payment cannot be partial.
Third Tuesday of May, meaning May 18 in 2027. Filing runs from May 1 to that day.

faqs.q: What if I never got a Brookhaven tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes, you owe the tax plus any penalties. If nothing has come by the third week of December, ring the Receiver of Taxes at 631-451-9009 and update your mailing address.
